claims.text: The baseline is an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy in a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
The baseline alloy has a target density below 6 g/cm3.
Spark plasma sintering of mechanically alloyed powders at 800-1000 °C can overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation.
Spark plasma sintering can improve room-temperature compressive behavior in Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
Spark plasma sintering can improve corrosion resistance in Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
Spark plasma sintering can improve resistance to high-temperature oxidation in Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
The proposed 800-1000 °C SPS range is below the vaporization point of magnesium.
Microstructure evolution, phase formation, and grain coarsening mediate the effects of SPS.
SPS may produce phases that improve the mechanical and corrosion properties of the alloy.
A controlled comparison of SPS-treated material with the as-processed baseline can test the proposed property improvements.
Failure to obtain a significant improvement in the tested properties would falsify the hypothesis.
